newsitem.title: VATICAN: Flu forces Pope to cancel audiences, rest.
newsitem.headline: Flu forces Pope to cancel audiences, rest.

text.p: Pope John Paul, suffering from influenza and a sore throat, unexpectedly cancelled audiences on Wednesday and was ordered to rest in bed.

"Influenza has entered even the Pope's house," he joked to thousands of pilgrims who had come to Rome to attend his general audience but had to settle instead for a brief appearance from his window overlooking St Peter's Square.

"The doctor has advised me not to go outdoors. He told me in particular to skip the Wednesday general audience," said the 76-year-old Pope, who has had a string of health problems in the past few years.
Despite the illness, the Pope's voice was clear and strong and he appeared in a good mood. He smiled and joked with the crowd about the rainy weather.

Vatican spokesman Joaquin Navarro-Valls said in a statement that the Pope was suffering from an inflammation of the throat and trachea (windpipe) which began on Tuesday night and was caused by influenza, which has been making the rounds in Rome.
"The Pope has been advised to rest in bed for a few days," the spokesman said.
It was not clear how much bed rest the Pope's personal doctor, Renato Buzzonetti, had ordered and the Vatican did not say whether he was taking medication.
Private audiences that had been scheduled for Thursday with Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar and Australian Foreign Minister Alexander Downer were also postponed.
The Polish Pontiff's recent health problems included surgery to remove a colon tumour in 1992, a hip replacement operation in 1994 and an operation last October to remove his appendix.
After years of effectively disobeying doctors' order to rest more the Pope has recently indicated that he is now prepared to listen to them.
When he left Rome's Gemelli hospital after the appendix operation, doctor's bluntly ordered history's most travelled Pope to rest more.
He has since delegated senior Vatican officials to preside at long religious services that would test his strength. He also has reduced the duration of individual private audiences.
Last Christmas the Pope skipped the Christmas morning mass so that he could rest after celebrating a long midnight mass in St Peter's Basilica.

On December 25, 1995, the world was alarmed when influenza forced the Pope to miss Christmas mass for the first time in his pontificate. Later that day nausea forced him to interrupt a televised address.
A fever which the Vatican said was of a "digestive nature" forced him to cancel public engagements in March 1996. A similar fever in August 1996 again forced him to cancel engagements.

The Vatican later said that all three episodes of fever in late 1995 and 1996 were caused by a recurring inflammation of the appendix. The discrepencies in official versions left some reporters sceptical.
An papal ailment that remains unexplained is his trembling left hand. The Vatican has not denied a string of media reports that the Pope is suffering from Parkinson's disease.
